question: The signal given by the policeman in the picture means
picture: Traffic policeman in white uniform and helmet with both arms raised straight up, palms facing forward

options.text: All vehicles must stop.
Vehicles approaching policeman from in front and behind him must stop.
Vehicles approaching from his right and left to stop.

question: This Police officer is signalling
picture: Traffic policeman in white uniform turned to the side with one hand raised, palm open

options.text: Drivers from his left, front and rear to go.
Drivers from his left, front and rear to stop.
Drivers from his right, front and behind to stop.

question: When a driver signals in this manner, it means
picture: Rear view of a blue car; driver's arm out of the right window moving in a circle (orange circular arrows)

options.text: He intends to make a U-turn.
He intends to go around the round-about.
He intends to move to the left or turn to the left.

question: You may overtake another vehicle on the left

options.text: If it is a heavy vehicle.
If the driver in front signals his intention to turn right.
If you are certain that the vehicle would not change direction.

question: When should you start to keep left after overtaking?

options.text: As soon as you are ahead of the overtaken vehicle.
When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your left wing mirror.
When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear view mirror inside the cabin.

question: This diagram shows Cars A, B and C turning in the directions indicated at an uncontrolled junction. Which car must give way?
picture: Top-down crossroads diagram with yellow Car A (bottom), blue Car B (right) and red Car C (top), curved arrows showing each car's turn

options.text: Car A must give way to cars B and C.
Car B must give way to cars A and C.
Car C must give way to cars A and B.

question: This diagram shows Cars A, B and C going in the directions indicated at an uncontrolled junction. Which cars should give way?
picture: Top-down crossroads diagram with yellow Car A (bottom), blue Car B (right) and red Car C (top); B's arrow goes straight, A's and C's arrows curve

options.text: Cars A and C should give way to Car B.
Cars A and B should give way to Car C.
Cars B and C should give way to Car A.

question: Driving with a 'bald' tyre is dangerous because

options.text: It skids more easily.
There is greater probability of punctures.
Both answers.

question: When you are driving along, you must check your rear view mirror once every

options.text: 1 to 2 seconds.
5 to 10 seconds.
20 to 30 seconds.

question: Reversing from a side road into a main road is

options.text: Allowed if there is no vehicle around.
Not allowed for it is unsafe and could cause road accident.
Allowed during the daytime only.

question: Crossing the double continuous white lines along the centre of the road

options.text: Is an offence because it is unsafe to do so.
Is not an offence if you are overtaking another vehicle.
Is not an offence if you do not cause inconvenience to others.

question: Your reaction time could be affected when

options.text: You are tired.
Your vehicle is old.
The traffic is heavy.

question: How does alcohol affect you?

options.text: It reduces your concentration.
It increases your awareness.
It improves your co-ordination.

question: Drink driving

options.text: Will not affect your reaction time.
May affect your reaction time.
May cause you to react faster.

question: Which of the following statements on alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive as long as you think you are not drunk.
It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol.
It is safe to drive one hour after having the last drink.

question: A person will be disqualified from driving if he is caught

options.text: Driving with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol/100ml of blood.
Failing to obey a 'Stop' traffic sign.
Failing to give way to an ambulance with its siren on.

question: When passing the stationary bus at the bus-stop, you should
picture: Video frame: red bus stopped in a yellow-marked bus bay with people at the stop; white car approaching from behind

options.text: Sound the horn to warn the bus driver of your presence.
Speed up to overtake the bus before it moves off.
Slow down and be ready to stop for pedestrian who may cross the road in front of the bus.

notes: Question text hyphenated across a line break ("bus-" / "stop"). Option C says "pedestrian" (singular) as printed.

question: When a car is stopping in front of a zebra crossing, you should
picture: Video frame: red car stopped before a zebra crossing with zigzag lines; pedestrians standing by the roadside

options.text: Quickly pass the vehicle before any pedestrians come along.
Sound the horn to warn pedestrians.
Slow down and be ready to stop for pedestrians to cross the road.

question: To check 'blind spot' when driving, you must

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Turn your head and look into the wing mirrors.
Turn your head and look into the rear-view mirror.

question: The 'Two-second Rule' is a sufficient distance between your vehicle and the car in front when road condition is

options.text: Wet.
Good.
Hazy.
